title: SAML connector interoperability patterns and test cases for Okta/Azure/Google/Ping
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures interoperability patterns, concrete mapping examples, and an executable test suite for SAML connectors with major IdPs (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, Ping). The goal is to produce a reviewable compatibility guide plus automated tests and troubleshooting recipes so SSO enablement for RBAC v2 customers is predictable and auditable.

Background:
We continue to observe subtle, IdP-specific behaviors that cause mis-mappings between SAML assertions and RBAC v2 claims: attribute name variations (email vs mail vs userPrincipalName), group encoding differences, NameID formats, signature/cert rotation practices, and assertion time skew handling. These cause 1) incorrect RBAC assignments, 2) noisy audit logs, and 3) confusing admin UX during onboarding.

Goals:
- Produce a compact set of mapping patterns that cover >95% of customer IdP configurations.
- Ship an automated test suite (integration + unit) that exercises binding, signature, NameID, attribute, and group mapping combinations against a staging connector.
- Update onboarding docs to include per-IdP quick-checks and a deterministic troubleshooting checklist.
- Ensure audit logging captures attribute->claim mappings and mismatch reasons for later postmortem and compliance exports.

Non-goals:
- Replacing customer-side IdP settings or implementing a full IdP simulator.
- Adding commercial IdP-specific UI flows beyond small per-IdP hints in Console.

Design/Patterns (high level):
1) Canonical claim set: define required/optional claims for RBAC v2 that the connector must produce: sub, email, preferred_username, name, groups (list), issued_at, expires_at, and assertion_id. Use fallback rules when fields are missing (see mapping table below).
2) Attribute normalization pipeline: string-normalize (lowercase emails), trim whitespace, collapse multi-valued attributes into sorted lists, support both CSV and repeated-attribute encodings for groups.
3) NameID handling: support three primary NameID formats and order of preference: emailAddress, persistent, unspecified. If NameID is present and matches email pattern, prefer it as sub/email.
4) Signature & cert rotation: accept multiple valid signing certs per IdP (configurable). On signature validation failure, emit a high-fidelity audit event containing IdP metadata, signature algorithm, and certificate thumbprint to help ops triage.
5) Time skew: allow configurable clock skew up to 5 minutes with clear audit entries when asserted timestamps are outside tolerance.

IdP-specific mapping notes (examples):
- Okta: groups often come via 'groups' or 'groups.display' attribute; SAML app may send either. Okta commonly sets NameID as email; test cases must cover both CSV and repeated group claims.
- Azure AD: email often in 'http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress' or 'upn' (userPrincipalName). Azure may omit groups when large (claims overage) and instead provide a 'hasGroups' flag — we must detect this and recommend SCIM or Graph-backed group sync for customers requiring full groups.
- Google Workspace: attributes may be in 'email' or 'primaryEmail'; groups often require separate provisioning APIs. Expect NameID=email and smaller group lists.
- Ping: legacy deployments sometimes use persistent NameIDs and non-standard attribute names like 'uid' or 'sAMAccountName'; mapping must support uid -> preferred_username fallback.

Mapping table (examples):
- sub: prefer NameID (if looks like unique id or email) -> 'uid' -> 'userPrincipalName' -> assertion 'subject'.
- email: 'email' -> 'mail' -> 'primaryEmail' -> NameID if RFC822.
- groups: 'groups' -> 'memberOf' -> CSV in 'groups' attribute -> repeated 'Group' attributes. Normalize casing and sort.

Acceptance Criteria (must be satisfied before release):
acceptance_criteria: Connector normalizes and emits canonical claim set for all four target IdPs in the staging environment.
Automated test harness covers 18 positive/negative SAML permutations (NameID formats, group encodings, signature rot, skew) and passes in CI.
Console onboarding doc updated with per-IdP quick-check checklist and sample SAML metadata snippets.
Audit logs include attribute->claim mapping with reason codes for any fallbacks or mismatches.
Security review sign-off obtained and release notes include known limitations and recommended mitigations.
test_plan: Unit tests for attribute normalization (email casing, trimming, CSV->list, repeated attrs).
Integration tests against local SAML IdP emulator for: Okta (CSV groups), Azure AD (overage flag), Google (primaryEmail), Ping (persistent NameID).
Signature rotation simulation: publish second cert to IdP metadata and verify connector accepts either cert when configured; emit audit entry when older cert used.
Time-skew tests at -6m, -3m, +4m to validate tolerance and audit logging behavior.
End-to-end RBAC mapping tests: given SAML with specific attributes, assert the resulting RBAC roles in staging and verify audit record contains mapping details.
rollout_plan: Merge connector changes behind a feature flag in staging.
Run nightly integration suite for 72 hours; if no regressions, enable limited beta for existing Dedicated customers and two pilot Hosted customers.
Collect telemetry for 7 days (mapping failure rate, audit event volume, onboarding friction score) and review in Weekly Security sync.
Gradual enablement to all customers with clear opt-out for those needing custom mapping.
monitoring: New audit event types: saml.mapping.fallback and saml.mapping.mismatch with payload fields: assertion_id, idp_entity_id, mapping_path, resolution_reason.
Dashboard: RBAC Mapping Failures by IdP (Okta/Azure/Google/Ping) with top 10 attribute mismatch examples.
Alert: if mapping failure rate > 0.5% for > 30 min for any IdP, page SSO on-call.
